title: Antimatter production scale-up and storage for propulsion
bottleneck: Antimatter annihilation is the most energy-dense reaction physically possible, theoretically enabling relativistic rockets — but humanity produces only nanograms per year at facilities like CERN, at astronomical cost, while one interstellar mission would need grams. Storage is equally hard: antiprotons must be suspended in electromagnetic Penning traps in perfect vacuum, since any contact with normal matter annihilates the fuel; no trap has held macroscopic quantities for mission-relevant durations.
why_it_blocks: Antimatter is the only known propellant with the energy density for conceivable relativistic crewed flight; without production scaled by many orders of magnitude and stable long-term storage, it stays in science fiction.
current_state: CERN's antimatter factory produces and traps small quantities for physics research. No propulsion program exists; only paper studies of antimatter-catalyzed concepts have been funded.
